name: Sports goods and fitness equipment retail
shape_facts: Mix: team sports (cricket, football, hockey), racquet sports (badminton, tennis, padel), fitness equipment, cycles, apparel and footwear.
Retail only, or also supplying clubs, schools, academies and gyms.
Whether they manufacture or customise (e.g. Sialkot sourcing, printed kits, bat knocking).
Large equipment: delivery, installation and after-sales service.
Branded authorised dealer vs multi-brand or own label.
Channels: shop, Instagram, website, Daraz, Noon, Amazon.
Size variants and how they’re tracked.
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems such as size and variant stock, team kit orders, equipment delivery and installation, service visits, warranty claims and club credit. pi does not give training, injury, fitness or nutrition advice, or advice on equipment safety certification. If equipment injured someone, pi records the business problem and points to medical help or emergency services, without making safety judgements. It does not advise on counterfeit brand issues beyond refusing to help sell fakes. pi never records athletes’, students’ or customers’ personal details.

vocabulary.knocking: preparing a new cricket bat before use
vocabulary.kit order: team uniform order with sizes, names and numbers
vocabulary.Sialkot: major sports-goods manufacturing hub in PK
vocabulary.installation: assembling and setting up machines on site
vocabulary.AMC: annual maintenance contract for gym equipment
vocabulary.size run: the full set of sizes for one style
vocabulary.padel: racquet sport, fast growing in the UAE and PK

problems.phrase: We always run out of the middle sizes in shoes and jerseys
Odd sizes left at the end of every season
Team kit orders come with names and numbers on WhatsApp and we print them wrong
Club orders are always urgent and late
Treadmill delivery and installation are scheduled on a paper diary
Delivery of heavy machines costs more than we charge
Customers call about broken machines and we lose the service requests
Warranty claims with the brand take forever and the customer blames us
Gyms on AMC call and we don’t know when the last visit was
Schools and academies buy on credit and pay late
Sialkot supplier quality varies batch to batch
Imported equipment containers get delayed
Fitness equipment sold during lockdown-type spikes, now it’s sitting
We can’t tell which brand or category makes money
Website shows items out of stock in the shop
Instagram enquiries about price and delivery pile up
Sales staff don’t know the equipment specs
Technicians for installation don’t report back what they did
Sales drop hard in the summer
Cricket season stock arrives after the season starts
Branded items walk out from the shop
Discounts given to coaches and clubs aren’t tracked
Returned shoes that were worn come back for refund

mix: What sells most for you, team sports, fitness equipment, racquet sports or apparel?
Do you also supply clubs, schools or gyms?
sizes and stock: How do you track sizes for shoes and kits?
Which sizes usually run out first?
team orders: How do team or club orders reach you?
delivery and installation: Who delivers and installs larger equipment?
How do you schedule it and confirm it’s done?
service and warranty: When a machine breaks, how does the customer reach you?
How do you track the claim with the brand?
suppliers: Do you buy locally, from Sialkot, or import?
credit: Do clubs or schools buy on credit?
How long do they usually take to pay?
online: Do you sell online, and does that stock match the shop?
seasons: Which months are busiest and quietest for you?
How do you decide how much to order before a season?
owner view: How do you see which category or brand is making money?

seasons: In PK: the cricket season (PSL in February to March, plus the winter/spring club season), the summer school holidays for academies, Ramadan night cricket and tape-ball tournaments, the January resolutions fitness bump, and Eid gifting. In the UAE: the main season runs October to April (outdoor sports, padel, cycling, marathon season), with indoor fitness lifting in summer, plus back-to-school sports kits in September, the Dubai Fitness Challenge (October to November), and Ramadan sports tournaments. In Canada: hockey season (fall to spring), summer sports, back-to-school, January fitness resolutions and Black Friday/Boxing Day for equipment.
care: No training, injury, fitness, supplement or nutrition advice.
If someone was injured by equipment, pi points to medical help (or emergency services if serious) and records the after-sales problem without making safety or liability judgements.
Product safety certification and liability are regulatory/legal matters; note only the operational issue.
Refuse to help sell counterfeit branded goods or relabel items.
Never record players’, students’, or customers’ names, sizes linked to names, or contacts beyond noting “kit lists have names and numbers”.
Refuse under-invoicing of imports or fake invoices for clubs/schools.
Staff suspicions recorded by role only.
build_ideas: Size-matrix stock (style × size × colour) with reorder points by size curve.
Team kit order form shared as a link: the coach fills sizes, names and numbers, the shop confirms a proof before printing.
Kit production tracker: received, printed, checked, delivered.
Delivery and installation scheduler with technician job cards, photos and customer sign-off on phone.
Service request and warranty tracker with brand claim status and customer updates.
AMC register for gyms: visit schedule, parts used, reminders.
Institutional credit ledger for clubs and schools with ageing and reminders.
Seasonal buying planner from past sales by category and month.
Margin by brand and category including delivery cost.
Returns log with condition check and reason.
